differences.title: 1. Architecture
differences.leftDesc: NebulaGraph employs a distributed, multi-leader architecture with separate storage and compute nodes for independent scaling and high availability.
differences.rightDesc: Neo4j typically uses a single leader for writes, with replicas for reads, and offers Causal Clustering for fault tolerance and scalability.

differences.title: 2. Data Model
differences.leftDesc: NebulaGraph uses a property graph model where nodes and edges can have arbitrary properties, enabling flexible data representation.
differences.rightDesc: Neo4j also uses the property graph model, with nodes having labels and properties, and relationships connecting them.

differences.title: 3. Query Language
differences.leftDesc: NebulaGraph's nGQL is inspired by SQL and Cypher, offering a familiar syntax with powerful graph traversal capabilities.
differences.rightDesc: Neo4j's Cypher is a declarative query language specifically designed for graphs, focusing on pattern matching.

differences.title: 4. Scalability
differences.leftDesc: NebulaGraph is designed for massive horizontal scalability, easily handling billions of edges and trillions of properties across many machines.
differences.rightDesc: Neo4j scales vertically by upgrading hardware and horizontally through read replicas and Causal Clustering for write availability.

differences.title: 5. ACID Compliance
differences.leftDesc: NebulaGraph prioritizes availability and performance, offering eventual consistency in its distributed setup, which can be tuned.
differences.rightDesc: Neo4j provides strong ACID compliance for transactions, ensuring data integrity and consistency, crucial for critical applications.

differences.title: 6. Storage Engine
differences.leftDesc: NebulaGraph leverages RocksDB for storage and Raft for consensus in its distributed mode, optimizing for performance and resilience.
differences.rightDesc: Neo4j uses its own custom storage engine with MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) to handle concurrent transactions efficiently.

differences.title: 7. Use Cases
differences.leftDesc: NebulaGraph excels in scenarios requiring massive datasets, real-time analytics, and high-throughput graph queries across distributed environments.
differences.rightDesc: Neo4j is ideal for applications needing intricate relationship analysis, fraud detection, recommendation engines, and identity management.
